title: Syllabus
text:
Everything in this course builds toward one skill — running a complete Bayesian analysis end to end. The take-home exam is exactly that, on a dataset you’ll meet at the end. You see the whole workflow in week 1 and deepen it each week.











#
Step
What you produce




1
DAG + estimand
The causal/associational question stated as a target quantity; a DAG.


2
Data summary
The data described: measurement, coverage, obvious issues.


3
Formal model
Likelihood + priors written down (the generative model).


4
Prior predictive check
Simulate from priors; confirm they imply plausible data.


5
Fit
Estimate with brms; weakly-informative priors by default.


6a
MCMC diagnostics
R-hat, ESS, divergences, trace plots — did sampling work?


6b
Posterior predictive check
Does the fitted model reproduce key features of the data?


7
Interpretation
Answer the estimand on the outcome scale, with uncertainty.


8
Limitations
What the analysis can and cannot support; threats and next steps.



This is the exam. Every homework exercises the steps introduced so far, cumulatively.

title: Syllabus
text:
Homework & feedback policy

A sample solution is published for every homework. Individual feedback is not provided by default — with one exception.
Opt-in AI feedback. If you add an open-source license.md to your submission repo, you opt in to automated, individualized feedback: an AI reads your submission alongside the sample solution and writes a FEEDBACK.qmd / FEEDBACK.pdf back into your repo. No license.md, no processing. This is entirely optional.

text:

Attendance and homework completion thresholds are published on the Schedule.
Homework completion is tracked automatically from your submission repos — submit on the org.

title: QMIR — Quantitative Methods
text:
How this course works

Weekly slides — linked from the Schedule.
Weekly homeworks — distributed through the course GitHub org; each ships with a sample solution published after the due date.
A final take-home exam — a complete 8-step Bayesian analysis. You see the target from week 1; every week builds toward it.

title: QMIR — Quantitative Methods
text:
Feedback policy — please read

A sample solution is published for every homework. Individual feedback is NOT provided by default. The only individual feedback available is the optional AI feedback you can opt into by adding an open-source license.md to your submission repo. See the Syllabus for details.

title: Installation Guide
text: What you need to do the homeworks and the exam.

title: Installation Guide
text:
Toolchain

R (recent release) and RStudio (or your editor of choice).
Quarto — https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/.
A LaTeX engine for PDF output: quarto install tinytex.
Git and a GitHub account — all homeworks and the exam are distributed and submitted through the course GitHub org.
Key R packages: tidyverse, brms (and its Stan backend), posterior, bayesplot, marginaleffects. Follow the in-class setup for the Stan toolchain.

title: Installation Guide
text:
Submitting

Open the homework link on the Schedule. It opens GitHub’s create from template page — make your own copy of the starter repo.
Name it exactly hw-NN-<username> (e.g. hw-03-jdoe, with your own GitHub username) and create it in the course organisation. The tracker finds submissions by that name; a repo named anything else is invisible to it.
Do your work in that repo, commit, and push. Rendering the PDF and pushing is your submission.
Opt-in feedback: add an open-source license.md to the repo to receive automated feedback (see Syllabus).
